page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-96-lssd is a memory-optimized and storage-intensive server instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The memory configuration provides 744 GB of RAM, yielding 7.75 GB of memory per core. For local storage, the instance includes 16 bundled NVMe SSDs totaling 6,167 GB of capacity, with no integrated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier performance across multiple domains. The system achieves top 10% placement in Passmark CPU tests, including database operations, physics, and encryption, alongside high-speed Redis SET operations at 170.8 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally strong, reaching 7,676.9 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 356.43 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Single-core performance is average in stress-ng, but multi-core execution is strong, supported by a 504 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-96-lssd offers high resource density by combining massive memory capacity with high-speed local NVMe storage on a single node, reducing the need for external storage attachments. This hardware profile is highly suitable for memory-heavy and I/O-demanding workloads, such as large-scale relational databases, in-memory data stores like Redis, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference prompt processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-96-lssd is a memory-optimized and storage-intensive server instance designed for demanding enterprise workloads. It is equipped with 96 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor running at 2.3 GHz, 744 GB of RAM, and 6,167 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across 16 drives. The architecture supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel AMX and AVX-512. In benchmark testing, the instance delivers top-tier performance in database operations, Redis throughput, and software compilation, alongside strong multi-core CPU capabilities and high memory bandwidth. This configuration is highly efficient for resource-dense deployments, eliminating the latency of external storage. It is best suited for large-scale databases, in-memory caching, and data-intensive processing tasks.
